question: with the address generated by the 19.2r byte-match route instead of the mean-pooled vector, and with zero training, does the store recognise its own paraphrases while the never-written classes fall behind?
sequence: instantiate ByteMatchRoute at identity, verify byte_embed = eye and weights = 1
build the real-forward store with today's write path (30 sentences, 32 slots)
record each write's address through the route (offset, score, nearest line)
read the 154-query battery twice: mean-key arm and byte-route arm, same store
run the frozen copy gate on the 22 correction faces
apply the pre-written verdict rule once

criteria.B1_route_is_the_primitive: the address is produced by ByteMatchRoute at its 19.2r initialisation: byte_embed equals eye(257, 256) exactly, position_weight equals 1 exactly, 0 updates, 0 optimizer steps; the free-offset search is the route's own (no injected offsets)
criteria.B2_one_variable: both arms read the same store: store keys, values, ages and count are byte-identical before and after every reading; only the read address differs (mean key vs byte route)
criteria.B3_battery: identical 154-query battery as the closed encoding line (22 paraphrases, 66 unwritten wordings, 3 negative classes of 22); the no_value class is a key-space midpoint with no textual form, so it has no byte query and is reported as not applicable
criteria.B4_written_primary: written face count = the write-back read: query the stored sentence itself, correct iff the winning line is the slot that sentence was written to
criteria.B5_gaps: the floor used for the class gaps is the minimum normalised alignment over the 22 paraphrases; the write-back floor is reported separately because it equals the maximum attainable score by construction and cannot test recognition
criteria.B6_gate_frozen: the copy gate is not modified and not retuned; its input remains the frozen mean key, so its verdict on the 22 correction faces is reported as inherited, not as caused by the byte address
criteria.V1_holds: written write-back >= 20 AND unwritten >= 60 AND at least two byte-expressible negative classes have a strictly positive gap AND the copy gate no longer refuses the 22 faces
criteria.V2_not_discriminative: every byte-expressible negative class has a normalised maximum >= 0.85 (near one) AND no class has a strictly positive gap: any two sentences of this template align about equally
criteria.V3_inconclusive: anything else: report the distributions only, no partial success
criteria.unchanged: no fixture, face, position, class, span or threshold is retuned after the first reading
